title: Scalar filters preserved spectral loop phases in passive models of two partial adult worm maps
abstract: We tested a spectral loop check in reciprocal passive models of two partial adult worm electrical maps. Each model had 180 cells, with 60 observed cells. Scalar low-pass filters, gains and delays changed pair phases but preserved triangle loop phases to within 7e-16. Equal independent source noise gave a zero loop sine. At a noise variance ratio bounded by two and angular frequency one, the median mean absolute loop sine over 50 noise patterns was 0.01824 and 0.01366. A deterministic 1% relative cross-spectrum error bound certified a non-real loop product in median shares of 18.87% and 10.77% of qualifying triangles. The error bound was added after the first run. A separate three-cell example had irreversible dynamics but zero loop phase. Thus nonzero loop phase can reject a reversible latent process under diagonal filtering, but zero loop phase cannot establish reversibility. These are exact population model results, not measured worm activity or finite-record detection rates. Partial anatomy, assumed conductances and noise, one observed set, and absent activity data limit biological use. Original code, aggregate results, a figure and external retrieval instructions support reproduction.

display.caption: Pair phases changed under unequal scalar filters. Triangle loop phases were preserved in two reciprocal circuit models. Shading shows the 5th to 95th percentiles over 50 assumed noise patterns, not uncertainty across animals.
